text:
tasha: Heads-up 00Aster Health is asking if we can act as a direct drop-in replacement for their current vendor (HeliosAPI). They want minimal client changes and the same sync + async response shapes. They also sent a short security questionnaire, want answers by EOW. Can we run a POC?
diego: Short: yes, but we need to clarify two major compatibility dims: 1) request shape (Helios uses `context` + `meta` fields) and 2) async webhook callbacks for long jobs (their clients expect a webhook POST).
ben: +1. Also note Helios's streaming is chunked JSON (not SSE) and they include an `X-Helios-Req` header that clients rely on for idempotency. We'll need to either honor those headers or synthesize equivalents.
frank: Do we have a sample webhook payload? async behavior will change the whole flow.
tasha: Customer pasted examples (trimmed):

tasha: ```
POST /v2/complete
{
  "context": "Patient note: ...",
  "max_length": 400,
  "dedupe_token": "abc-123",
  "stream": false,
  "callback_url": "https://aster-callbacks.health/helios"
}
```

tasha: Expected async callback: ```
POST /helios-callback
{
  "job_id": "j-789",
  "status": "finished",
  "result": {"summary":"..."},
  "meta": {"request_id":"r-123"}
}
```

diego: Ok. Plan: we can implement a compatibility proxy that accepts Helios endpoints, translates requests to Redwood API calls, and if callback_url present, posts results back with Helios-shaped body. For streaming clients, we can chunk our SSE events into Helios chunked JSON lines.
ben: Security: Aster is HIPAA-covered. They need BAAs, KMS details, audit log retention, and mTLS for management endpoints. I'll coordinate with Priya for the questionnaire answers.
priya: FYI I started the questionnaire. We can provide SOC2 Type II and encryption details. Hosted customers get Redwood-managed KMS by default; Dedicated can use customer-managed keys. We'll need to confirm whether the customer wants Hosted with BAA or a Dedicated/private deployment.
frank: Technical parity note: Helios applies a postprocessing filter that removes PHI tokens based on heuristics. That will affect outputs. We can mirror that in the shim by running an extra postprocess step, but we should be explicit it's a best-effort match. Exact byte-level parity unlikely.
diego: For acceptance criteria: customer wants no "functional regressions" on clinical summaries. Suggest we propose: run N=250 canonical notes, measure F1 on key clinical entities + manual spot-checks. If regression under threshold X, we pass. Need to get them to agree on metrics.
tasha: Sales asks about pricing: they want preserved per-req price for 90 days and an option to convert to committed capacity. What flexibility do we have?
ben: We can offer a 90-day pilot credit that approximates their current unit cost; if they convert to Dedicated we can lock a committed rate. Finance needs numbers.
priya: Ops/security: question about auth model. Do we accept their Helios tokens directly? Hosted infra doesn't allow customer-supplied tokens. We can front with an auth-proxy that validates Helios tokens, mints ephemeral Redwood tokens, and logs mapping. Dedicated can accept their token if they manage the key.
diego: Also we need to map error codes: Helios returns 409 for duplicate dedupe tokens, 422 for parsing issues, 5xx some legacy codes. We'll need a mapping layer that translates our internal errors to Helios semantics.
frank: I'll prototype a minimal proxy (node/express) that handles request mapping, error mapping, and async callback fanout. ETA: 2 business days if I get curl samples and webhook signing secret.
tasha: customer provided a cURL and a webhook signing secret placeholder in doc. cURL: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer HELIOS_KEY" -d '{"context":"Note","max_length":300,"callback_url":"https://x"}' https://api.helios.ai/v2/complete```
ben: For telemetry and auditing, Aster insists on per-request audit entries including original Helios headers. We'll need to capture and persist those in audit logs for the pilot. Storage retention window: 7 years? they asked 7y for clinical audit logs. That might be an enterprise config. Priya, is that feasible?
priya: 7-year retention is an enterprise add-on. We can offer it, but will require a pricing delta and storage plan. I'll flag to GPO.
diego: Integration testing: propose a 3-step POC: 1) shim prototype + smoke tests (internal) 2) parity run (50 canonical notes) -> diff report + clinical QA 3) short production pilot (30 days) with routing fallback to Helios if drift detected.
frank: I'll push prototype to staging and post endpoint.

deploy-bot: deploy started by frank for branch integration/aster-compat at commit d4e5f - staging proxy: https://staging-proxy.redwood.net/helios/v2/complete

frank: staging up. basic sync + async flow tested. Need to fix webhook signature header (we currently send `x-redwood-signature` but Helios clients expect `x-helios-signature`).
diego: I'll update the proxy to copy headers and sign with supplied secret. Also will add idempotency header handling for dedupe_token.
priya: security-bot: Questionnaire submitted by priya. Items open: BAA draft, KMS key owner field, retention SLA, access control configs. Priya is the owner.
ben: action items: frank -> shim prototype (staging up), diego -> add header mapping + error mapping, priya -> questionnaire + BAA, tasha -> SOW draft and pricing request, sam (ops) -> prepare ephemeral token proxy design if Hosted.
tasha: thanks all 10:thumbsup: I'll update the customer with the proposed POC plan and ask them to confirm the canonical prompt set and the metric thresholds.
frank: will post staging logs and a sample cURL test in the thread in ~1h.
ben: finance note: we should propose a pilot credit instead of a deep discount to avoid setting list price precedents.
tasha: closing note: make sure we capture the client's webhook retry semantics and max concurrency expectations. They are very sensitive to duplicate callbacks.
frank: noted.
priya: I'll upload the questionnaire answers and BAA draft to the Aster folder: https://redwood-internal/company/aster/presales

tasha: perfect. follow-ups Monday morning unless something urgent comes up."
